newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil off on softer IPE gas oil, slack deman.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil off on softer IPE gas oil, slack deman.

text.p: NWE gas oil sank lower on Friday in line with weaker benchmark IPE futures and continuing slack demand, traders said.
June IPE settled $1.50 lower at $164.25 a tonne, while July ended $2.00 off at $165.75 a tonne.

Heating oil barges were done at June IPE +75 cents fob ARA for second half delivery storage material. There was talk that prompt running refinery had been done at June IPE +$1.0 fob Rotterdam but this was not confirmed.

Low sulphur barges were done in a similarly moribund state with premiums assessed at June IPE +$6.50/+$8.50 fob ARA althought nothing thought to have traded. "I was offering above $8.0 all day and got no response," said one trader.
On the cargo front, traders said the current contango on IPE gas oil was encouraging a number of players to put winter grade low sulphur material into storage if they had any available.
The September closed $5.25 above June gas oil at $169.50 a tonne, while the November contract ended $10 above at $174.25 a tonne.
